query: Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: goal_achieved
per_column.rationale: Binary per-record realization of the focus outcome (goal achievement), directly restates the target, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: completion_gap
per_column.rationale: Difference between completion and target; lies on the causal path to whether the goal is achieved (goal_achieved is essentially derived from this gap). Adjusting for it would block the effect, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: dept_goal_achievement_rate
per_column.rationale: Department-level aggregation of the outcome itself; it is the very quantity that differs across departments, not a cause of it.

per_column.name: dept_avg_target_pct
per_column.rationale: Departmental average target ambition is a candidate cause of achievement rates (harder targets lower achievement). A plausible treatment whose effect on the outcome is being attributed.

per_column.name: dept_avg_completion_pct
per_column.rationale: Average completion percentage is directly downstream of effort/targets and directly determines achievement; it sits on the causal path to the outcome, so it is a mediator.

per_column.name: dept_completion_rate
per_column.rationale: Rate of completed items is essentially a restatement/proxy of the outcome-generating mechanism, on the path to achievement rather than a common cause.

per_column.name: dept_cancellation_rate
per_column.rationale: Departmental workflow/discipline reflected by cancellation rate can plausibly influence both how targets are set/pursued (treatment) and achievement (outcome); surfaced from data, not named in query. Weakly a common cause; could also be partly downstream.

per_column.name: dept_high_priority_rate
per_column.rationale: Share of high-priority goals reflects departmental work portfolio, which can affect both the ambition of targets set (treatment) and achievability (outcome). Not named in the query; a plausible common cause, though partly a treatment-like exposure itself.

judge.rationale: The set does supply a plausible treatment (dept_avg_target_pct) and a couple of department-context variables (cancellation rate, high-priority rate) that were NOT named in the query and could act as common causes of both target-setting behaviour and achievement, demonstrating some genuine surfacing. However, the design is dominated by outcome restatements (goal_achieved, dept_goal_achievement_rate) and mediators on the causal path (completion_gap, dept_avg_completion_pct, dept_completion_rate). These completion-based columns are essentially the mechanism by which goals are achieved, so labelling them as adjustment variables would be a mistake. The identified confounders are only weakly established as common causes and are themselves partly exposure-like, so confounder quality is low. Overall the augmentation leans toward describing/aggregating the outcome rather than setting up an unbiased causal estimation with clearly adjusted, query-independent confounders.
